title: Bounds on K(8,1,2), the first unknown term of OEIS A004045
description:
Artifacts for lower bounds on binary multiple covering codes.

K(n,R,mu) is the minimum size of a binary code in F_2^n such that every word has at least mu codewords within Hamming distance R. K(8,1,2) is the first unknown term of OEIS A004045; the published record is 59 <= K(8,1,2) <= 64.

An elementary parity/excess argument shows that for even n, |C| >= ceil(3 * 2^(n+1) / (3n+2)). This strictly improves the best published lower bound at five table positions (n = 8, 10, 12, 14, 16) and reproves the exact value K(6,1,2) = 20 without computer search. In particular K(8,1,2) >= 60, established by three independent routes: the theorem, an exact-rational SCIP to VIPR certificate refuting |C| = 59 accepted by viprchk, and exhaustive numerical verification.

Also included, explicitly as a candidate without human review: a refutation of |C| = 60 that would give K(8,1,2) >= 61, and a Lean 4 formalisation of it whose statements typecheck but whose proofs are unfinished.

The upper bound 64 (Oestergaard 1995) is unchanged by this work.
